features.label: Connection transport (ICE / DTLS)

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Implement DTLS restart.

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Create MediaPacket before firing signals.

patches.author: Nicolas Grunbaum
patches.subject: do not use magic numbers;r=dbaker

patches.author: Nicolas Grunbaum
patches.subject: run clippy on mdns_service;r=dbaker

patches.author: Nicolas Grunbaum
patches.subject: make gecko-profiler optional for mdns_service;r=dbaker

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Stop passing around munged remote candidates.

features.summary: WebRTC connections can now perform a DTLS restart, refreshing the encrypted transport without rebuilding the whole call. ICE candidate handling was simplified so remote candidates are passed in their original form, while media packets are prepared before connection signals are sent, making connection state changes more reliable.

features.label: WebRTC tests

patches.author: Daniel Baker
patches.subject: Force-enable tab sharing pref in getUserMedia source telemetry test

patches.author: Michael Froman
patches.subject: Remove reftest-wait even when getDisplayMedia() rejects.

patches.author: Daniel Baker
patches.subject: Record the actually granted getUserMedia source

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Make RTCSessionDescription.type/sdp readonly.

patches.author: Anna Weine
patches.subject: Don't send the ML-KEM key share for WebRTC DTLS by default

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Negotiate the dependency descriptor RTP header extension for receiving video.

features.summary: These tests improve coverage for screen and tab sharing, getUserMedia source telemetry, rejected getDisplayMedia() calls, and fire-and-forget play() promises. They also verify WebRTC API immutability, avoid sending ML-KEM key shares by default in DTLS, and test receiving video with the dependency descriptor RTP header extension, which helps describe frame dependencies for video processing.

features.label: WebRTC

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Only report a capture frame size change when it actually changed.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Plumb H264 profile and level into WebrtcGmpVideoCodec.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Constrain WebRTC video encoder resolution/framerate to the negotiated H264/AV1 level (both codecs).

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Make MediaCapabilities validate AV1 fmtp params.

features.summary: WebRTC now carries H.264 profile and level information through its video encoder and limits H.264 and AV1 resolution and frame rate to what the negotiated codec level supports. MediaCapabilities also validates AV1 format parameters more accurately, while capture changes are reported only when the frame size truly changes.

features.label: libwebrtc integration

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Report H264 QP thresholds from WebrtcMediaDataEncoder so libwebrtc's QualityScaler can track it.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Serialize MediaCapabilities encode-support probes through an encoder AllocPolicy.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Add PEMFactory::StrictSupportsAsync and strict WebRTC encode support path for MediaCapabilities.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Add strict create-and-probe WebRTC decode support path for MediaCapabilities.

features.summary: MediaCapabilities now performs stricter, real encoder and decoder capability checks for WebRTC instead of relying only on broad assumptions. Encoder probes are serialized safely, and H.264 quality thresholds are exposed so libwebrtc’s QualityScaler can better adjust video quality to current conditions.

features.label: Camera & audio capture

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Apply capture rotation centrally, behind a pref.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Don't swap the requested frame dimensions for rotated frames.

features.summary: Camera frame rotation is now applied in one central capture path, behind a preference, so different capture backends behave consistently. Requested width and height are preserved rather than being swapped just because the camera reports rotated frames.

features.label: Negotiation engine (JSEP)

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Populate and correctly negotiate AV1 fmtp parameters in jsep.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Merge directions when an RTP header extension is registered again with a different direction.

features.summary: The WebRTC negotiation engine now populates and negotiates AV1 format parameters (fmtp), including codec profile and level details. Re-registering an RTP header extension with a new direction now combines the directions correctly instead of losing part of the negotiation.

features.label: Session negotiation (SDP)

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Fix AV1 fmtp profile/level-idx parsing bugs in the sipcc and rsdparsa SDP parsers.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Fix stale AV1 RTP spec anchors in comments.

features.summary: SDP parsing now correctly handles AV1 fmtp profile and level-index parameters in both of Firefox’s WebRTC parsers, improving interoperability with peers that advertise AV1 capabilities. The accompanying documentation references were refreshed; _there is no intended visible change by itself_.

features.label: WebRTC web API (RTCPeerConnection)

patches.author: Philipp Hancke
patches.subject: suppress dtls error on ice failures

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Exclude AV1's asymmetric profile fmtp parameter from RTCRtpSender's codec dictionary match.

features.summary: WebRTC no longer reports a misleading DTLS error when the underlying ICE connection fails, making connection failures easier to interpret. Codec matching also treats AV1’s asymmetric profile parameter correctly when comparing RTCRtpSender codec dictionaries.

features.label: Android camera capture

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Report rotation from the Android capture backend instead of applying it.

features.summary: On Android, the camera capture backend now reports the camera’s rotation directly instead of Firefox rotating the frames afterward. This keeps orientation information tied to the platform source and avoids duplicate or inconsistent rotation handling.

features.label: Libwebrtc Overrides

patches.author: Jens Stutte
patches.subject: Use std::source_location in WebrtcLocation.

features.summary: WebRTC’s diagnostic location information now uses C++ std::source_location, allowing source file and line details to be captured by the language rather than maintained through custom arguments. This is an internal reliability and maintainability improvement with no expected user-facing change.

features.label: Session negotiation (SDP)

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Fix AV1 fmtp profile/level-idx parsing bugs in the sipcc and rsdparsa SDP parsers.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Fix stale AV1 RTP spec anchors in comments.

The SDP stack is also being moved from duplicated SIPCC-specific structures to shared Rust webrtc-sdp implementations, including common media sections, attributes, bandwidth handling, and the C API; _this is primarily an internal modernization_.

New tests cover Video Orientation RTP signaling and reception, early-media reoffers with MID-only demultiplexing, and rejected play() promises, helping Firefox handle real-world call setup and media controls more consistently.

features.summary: Firefox’s WebRTC codec checks are now more accurate and coordinated: MediaCapabilities, the web API that reports media support, uses strict create-and-probe tests and shared asynchronous checks for encoding and decoding. AV1, H.264, hardware encoders on Android, and WebRTC GMP plugins are handled more reliably, while QualityScaler can now use H.264 picture-quality data to adjust video quality. This helps websites choose codecs that Firefox can actually use and avoid failed calls or poor performance.

features.summary: The RTCPeerConnection WebRTC API received fixes for connection recovery, media negotiation, and frame handling. Codec preferences now reach the outgoing track, AV1 profile matching follows the standard more closely, Insertable DTMF behavior is more spec-compliant, and bundled connections can receive media earlier. These changes make video calls and real-time audio more dependable across different browsers and network conditions.

features.summary: Firefox’s WebRTC connection transport now supports DTLS restarts, allowing an encrypted connection to be refreshed without rebuilding the entire call. ICE candidate handling and mDNS service code were cleaned up, including safer failure behavior and clearer remote-candidate data. Together, these changes improve recovery and maintainability for the networking layer behind WebRTC calls.

features.summary: Camera capture now applies video rotation in one central place, controlled by a preference, while preserving the dimensions the website requested. New fake-camera patterns and pixel-level tests verify that rotated frames are correct, which is important for phones and other devices whose camera orientation changes. _The testing preference is not a user-facing feature._

features.summary: Firefox’s JSEP negotiation engine, which builds and interprets WebRTC session descriptions, now negotiates AV1 format parameters more correctly. It also handles repeated RTP header-extension registrations, early-media filtering, and tentative reception during reoffers more accurately. This reduces mismatches when calls are renegotiated or when browsers advertise different AV1 and RTP capabilities.

features.summary: WebRTC video handling now carries H.264 profile and level information through the GMP codec path and limits H.264 and AV1 encoding to the resolution and frame rate those negotiated levels allow. MediaCapabilities also validates AV1 format parameters, while capture events are reported only when the frame size truly changes. These updates help prevent unsupported video settings and make codec negotiation more predictable.

features.summary: Firefox’s vendored libwebrtc build was updated for version 154 tooling and made quieter and more robust with newer Clang releases. The build scripts now give clearer messages when an upstream commit cannot be found, and an unnecessary compiler warning in Abseil was silenced. _These are build-process changes with no intended user-visible feature change._

features.summary: On Android, the camera capture backend now reports the camera’s rotation directly instead of Firefox rotating the frames afterward. This keeps orientation information tied to the platform source and avoids duplicate or inconsistent rotation handling.

features.summary: WebRTC’s diagnostic location information now uses C++ std::source_location, allowing source file and line details to be captured by the language rather than maintained through custom arguments. This is an internal reliability and maintainability improvement with no expected user-facing change.
